binders: An arbitrary natural number n, implicitly quantified, with no positivity restriction.
Arbitrary real numbers ug, um, ua, etaR, and rhoA.
Arbitrary functions AMRinv, AMRinvInv, MR, MRinv, A, and Ainv of type Fin n to Fin n to Real, equivalently six arbitrary real n by n matrices.
conclusions: B = E if and only if um = 0, etaR = 0, or K(MR,MRinv) = 0.
If um > 0, etaR > 0, and K(MR,MRinv) > 0, then B < E.
mathematical_definitions: For a real n by n matrix X, let N(X) denote the matrix norm selected by Matrix.instL2OpNormedAddCommGroup, the supplied L2 operator matrix norm.
For matrices X and Y, define K(X,Y) = N(X) * N(Y).
Define B = ug * K(AMRinv,AMRinvInv) * K(MR,MRinv) + ua * K(A,Ainv) * rhoA.
Define E = (ug * K(AMRinv,AMRinvInv) * K(MR,MRinv) + um * etaR * K(MR,MRinv)) + ua * K(A,Ainv) * rhoA.

The exact increment is Delta = um * etaR * K(MR,MRinv), so real associativity and commutativity give E = B + Delta. Since norms are nonnegative, K(MR,MRinv) >= 0, and the two hypotheses imply Delta >= 0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, all five real scalar parameters, and all six real n by n matrices, assume that um and etaR are nonnegative. The augmented quantity E is the baseline quantity B plus exactly um times etaR times the product of the norms of MR and MRinv. Consequently E is at least B. Equality holds exactly when at least one of um, etaR, or that norm product is zero; if all three factors are strictly positive, then E is strictly greater than B.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem makes no assertion for parameter choices with um < 0 or etaR < 0, because its required nonnegativity hypotheses then cannot be supplied.
The dimension n may be zero. In that case Fin n is empty and the matrix space contains only the zero matrix, so the relevant norm products vanish.
Despite their identifiers, AMRinvInv, MRinv, and Ainv are not assumed to be inverses of any other matrices. No matrix multiplication or inverse equation occurs.
No matrix is assumed nonsingular, nonzero, symmetric, positive definite, or otherwise structured.
The scalars ug, ua, and rhoA are unrestricted and may be negative, so B and E themselves need not be nonnegative; only their increment is forced to be nonnegative.
The strict conclusion is an implication and is vacuous whenever any of its three positivity premises fails.
The equality criterion uses the aggregate condition K(MR,MRinv) = 0 rather than explicitly stating which matrix norm is zero.
All operations are exact operations on mathematical real numbers. No floating-point operation, rounding model, approximation, or error semantics is encoded.
There are no existentially quantified witnesses or uniqueness claims.
ambiguities: The packet does not unfold Matrix.l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.toNorm to an entrywise or supremum formula, so the norm is identified exactly by the supplied matrix L2-operator-norm instance rather than by an independently expanded formula.
